title: vtree2
text: Imagine disease test disease. good test? can consider often test makes error infected subject, incorrectly giving negative result. called false negative (FN). probability error called false negative rate (FNR), compliment sensitivity: sensitive test , less likely test result negative person sick. Let’s assume test highly sensitive, example FNR 2% (making sensitivity 98%). Another type error healthy subject, test showing positive. value number false positives (FP) divided total number healthy people, also known FPR - false positive rate. complement value (1−FPR1 - FPR) called specificity. Say, outstanding test specificity 98%, false positive rate 2%. OK, story. Whether positive test result corresponds real patient false positive depends likely person actually healthy reality. disease prevalence, often disease encountered people tested. Say, disease quite common, prevalence 2%. , assuming performed screening tests 5^{4} persons population, get following table: can build data: can visualize table vtree. Since frequency table, need use vtree_from_freqtable() function1. starters, show Status first, Test result. show us many healthy persons incorrectly classified positive, many infected persons incorrectly classified negative.  can see, percentages leaf nodes (right side plot) correspond FPR FNR values. percentages internal nodes correspond disease prevalence. inverse question? fraction healthy people among tested positive, vice versa - fraction infected people among tested negative?  see among tested negative, large majority (practically 100%) indeed healthy. negative predictive value (NPV) test. However, among tested positive, 50% actually infected. positive predictive value (PPV) test shows despite test specific sensitive, person positive test result, 50% chance person actually healthy.
code: FPR <- .02 # p that healthy is positive FNR <- .02 # p that infected is negative prevalence <- 1/50  N <- 50000  data <- tribble(  ~ Status, ~ Test, ~ N,  "Infected", "Positive", round(prevalence * N * (1-FNR)),  "Infected", "Negative", round(prevalence * N * FNR),  "Healthy",  "Positive", round((1 - prevalence) * N * FNR),   "Healthy",  "Negative", round((1 - prevalence) * N * (1 - FNR))  ) vt <- vtree_from_freqtable(data,                            Status, Test,                            .freq_col = "N") plot(vt) vt2 <- vtree_from_freqtable(data,                            Test, Status,                            .freq_col = "N") plot(vt2)

text: vtree2, workflow split several steps: Prepare data (outside vtree2) Build vtree object vtree() vtree_from_freqtable() (Optional) Prune, retain select nodes prune(), retain() friends. (Optional) Create summaries summary_vt(). (Optional) Add modify labels add_labels() mutate(). (Optional) Add modify colors add_palette() mutate(). Plot vtree plot(). example demonstrating steps based titanicNA data set. data set Titanic data set, missing values randomly added demonstration purposes.
code: data(titanicNA)  vtree(titanicNA, Class, Sex, Survived) |>   # only retain the third class passengers   retain(path == "Class:3rd") |>   # add default labels   add_labels() |>   # change the labels for the missing values   mutate(label = gsub("NA", "Missing", label)) |>   # add colors   add_palette(palettes = c("Greys", "Blues", "Purples"),               na_fill = "grey90") |>   # change the color for Females who survived   # mark() is a helper function that returns TRUE for the nodes that   # match the given condition   mark(path == "Class:3rd/Sex:Female/Survived:Yes") |>   mutate(fill = ifelse(mark, "red", fill)) |>   mutate(color = ifelse(mark, "white", color)) |>   # plotting with legend and custom margins   plot(legend = TRUE,        margins = c(0.05, 0.05, 0.25, 0.05))

Alternatively, can call function add_layout() directly vtree object. resulting vtree contains additional columns x, y, width height nodes x1, y1, x2, y2 edges. can modify columns directly. following example modify layout pruned nodes. move nodes right (leafs) hand bit upwards.  Note mutate edges .edge = TRUE argument. different tidygraph, object (tree) can either activated “node” “edge” mode. vtree2, object always “node” mode (practical), rare occassion need access edges, can. add_layout() function additional parameters: varspace varsize. can assign amount relative space available node depending variable associated . example, might want show long summary takes lot space leafs, short labels internal nodes. can tune relative node sizes two parameters.
